claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with a thin copper interlayer improves the tungsten–copper interface quality.
Improving the tungsten–copper interface by copper pre-coating increases the composite's overall thermal conductivity.
Copper pre-coating retains the mechanical durability of the W–Cu composite.
Copper pre-coating retains the irradiation resistance of the W–Cu composite.
Pre-coating produces an improved, continuous copper interlayer at the tungsten surface.
A continuous copper interlayer reduces tungsten–copper interfacial thermal resistance.
A continuous copper interlayer minimizes defects at the tungsten–copper interface.
Copper pre-coating provides a more uniform heat-conduction pathway.
Thermal interface resistance is a key factor limiting heat transport in composites.
The continuity and purity of the copper interlayer preserve mechanical integrity by avoiding damage-prone defects present at untreated interfaces.
The continuity and purity of the copper interlayer preserve irradiation resistance by avoiding damage-prone defects present at untreated interfaces.
A W–Cu composite made with copper-pre-coated tungsten particles will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable composite made without pre-coating.
The pre-coated composite's mechanical durability will be at least unchanged relative to the uncoated control.
The pre-coated composite's irradiation resistance will be at least unchanged relative to the uncoated control.
The predicted improvement should hold under elevated temperatures, cyclic thermal loads, and irradiation exposure representative of heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications.
